solutions.check: 30 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: Transport stimulant

blocks.note: first meaning: rapture, being carried away by emotion
second meaning: the street name for the drug MDMA

explanation.walkthrough: 'Transport' looks like buses and trains, but here it is the old sense of overwhelming joy, as in 'transports of delight'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecstasy is both intense rapture and the popular name of a party drug that stimulates users.

clue.text: Opponent making Tory an offer

blocks.note: Con is short for Conservative, the Tory party
a tender is a formal offer, as for a contract

explanation.surface: A rival politician makes the Conservatives a proposal.
explanation.walkthrough: CON is the standard short form of Conservative, and a tender is a bid or offer.
explanation.definitionFit: A contender is a rival competing against you, so an opponent in a contest or election.

clue.text: Plot involving two Tory heads holding back interest rate

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, so only the front of the word is kept
going back means running the letters in the opposite direction
to hold something is to keep it in your grip, so the outer letters wrap round the inner ones

blocks.note: the first letter of Tory, taken twice
CAR is the compound annual rate of interest

explanation.surface: A Conservative scheme in which two party leaders hold down interest rates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plot' looks like a conspiracy, but it is a plot of land. CAR stands for compound annual rate, a measure of interest.
explanation.definitionFit: A tract is an area or expanse of land, the same as a plot in the sense of ground.

clue.text: Island star turn, Katie starts getting tits out

indicators.note: the start of each word is its first letter, so only those initials are kept
something put out of place is disordered, so its letters get rearranged

blocks.note: initials of the three words
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A tabloid headline: a celebrity called Katie, the star turn on an island holiday, goes topless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starts' covers all three words before it, not just Katie. The cheeky surface is typical of Private Eye.
explanation.definitionFit: St Kitts is a Caribbean island, one half of the nation of Saint Kitts and Nevis.

clue.text: Trump's odd love for masculine energy? Attitude that's just for effect

indicators.note: one thing given for another is a swap, so one letter takes another's place
something odd is out of the ordinary, so the letters fall into an unusual order

blocks.note: the name with its possessive S
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O
M is the abbreviation for masculine; it is the letter swapped out
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Trump's strange fondness for macho energy is just an act put on for show.
explanation.walkthrough: Put O in place of the M in TRUMPS to get TRUOPS, add E, and rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A posture can be a pose or stance adopted for show rather than sincerely held, an affected attitude.

clue.text: (& 23dn.) Potty item placed under orifice for start of booze session?

indicators.note: potty means crazy, so the letters go haywire into a new order
in a down answer, putting one piece under another sets it later in the word

blocks.note: an orifice is a hole or opening
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A potty is put beneath a bodily hole, a lavatorial image dressed up as a drinking question.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, 'placed under' puts the rearranged word below the synonym for orifice. In Britain, pubs once had strict legal hours, so opening time was when drinking could begin.
explanation.definitionFit: Opening time is the hour a pub opens its doors and starts serving drinks.

clue.text: Clover-like, shambolic Tories almost fled

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped
a shambolic thing is chaotic and disorganised, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the word without its final letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: A chaotic Conservative party nearly ran away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' trims only the party word; the verb stays whole before everything is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A trefoil is a three-leaved plant like clover, or an ornament of that shape, so trefoiled describes something with that form.

clue.text: Filthy Conservative is ditched, looking rather red

indicators.note: to ditch something is to get rid of it, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: cruddy means dirty or disgusting
C is the abbreviation for Conservative

explanation.surface: A dirty Tory is dumped and left looking flushed.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove C from CRUDDY.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruddy describes a healthy reddish complexion, a face with a fresh red glow.

clue.text: Exuberant former TV presenter knocked off gig economy company?

indicators.note: things knocked off are removed, so those letters are taken away

blocks.note: taken as written
an ex is a former partner, so ex means former
Ant McPartlin, of the British TV duo Ant and Dec

explanation.surface: A lively ex-TV host gets fired from a ride-hailing app job.
explanation.walkthrough: Ant and Dec are a hugely popular British presenting pair. Take EX and ANT out of EXUBERANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Uber is the ride-hailing firm whose drivers work as freelancers, the classic example of the gig economy.

clue.text: Powerless to grab woman's dress, like Boris?

indicators.note: to grab is to seize and hold, so one piece closes around another

blocks.note: unable means without the power to do something
a sack is a loose, shapeless dress

explanation.surface: A jibe at Boris Johnson as too helpless to resist grabbing a woman's clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by example: Boris Johnson long seemed to survive every scandal that would have ended other careers.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsackable means impossible to dismiss, which was how Boris Johnson's political survival looked during his scandals.

clue.text: see 24ac.
see 24ac.
Preserve time to sin with independent politician

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time
to err is to do wrong, to sin
I is the abbreviation for independent
a Tory is a Conservative politician

explanation.surface: Keep time free to misbehave with a maverick MP.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Preserve' looks like a verb, but it is the noun: an area kept for someone's exclusive use, as in a game preserve.
explanation.definitionFit: A preserve is a domain or area reserved for one person or group, exactly what a territory is.

clue.text: A day shift, one of Donald's regular ones?

blocks.note: taken as written
D is the abbreviation for day
a shift is a simple straight dress

explanation.surface: A day's work stint, presented as part of Donald Trump's routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shift' looks like a work period, but it is a garment. The definition is by example: Trump makes speeches constantly.
explanation.definitionFit: An address is a formal speech, and Donald Trump delivers them to rallies and the nation frequently.

clue.text: Jogger getting on new student

blocks.note: re means on or concerning
a fresher is a first-year university student in Britain

explanation.surface: A runner climbs aboard alongside a first-year undergraduate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jogger' suggests a runner, but it is a memory jogger, something that prompts recall.
explanation.definitionFit: A refresher reminds you of what you once knew, jogging the memory back into action.

clue.text: Twit collars retired member at end of debate – classic!

indicators.note: to retire is to go back or withdraw, so the letters run backwards
the end of a word is its final letter, the only one kept
to collar someone is to grab them round the neck, so one piece encloses another

blocks.note: an ass is a fool
a leg is a limb, a member of the body
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A fool grabs an elderly MP as a debate finishes, and the moment is a classic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member' and 'retired' suggest a pensioned-off MP, but the member is a limb, turned backwards and followed by E, all inside the fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Something classic never goes out of date and keeps its appeal for every generation, timeless in the same way.

clue.text: Glitter-like, with line in flashing

indicators.note: placing one thing in another means it sits inside it

blocks.note: sparking means giving off flashes
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: Something glittery with a line of flashing lights.
explanation.walkthrough: The single letter for line sits inside the word for flashing, after SPARK.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparkling describes surfaces that glitter with small points of shining light, as glitter does.

clue.text: Liberal in favour of Unite

blocks.note: pro means for or in favour of
to fuse is to join together

explanation.surface: A Liberal Democrat backs Unite, Britain's large trade union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liberal' looks like the political party and Unite like the trade union, but they are an adjective meaning generous and a verb meaning join.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberal can mean plentiful or lavish, as in liberal helpings, and profuse means abundant in the same way.

clue.text: Recruits go on the piss, led by Mark

blocks.note: a sign is a mark
to sup is to drink; going on the piss is British slang for a drinking bout

explanation.surface: New army recruits go out drinking, with a man called Mark leading them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Led by' puts the mark first. Mark looks like a man's name, but it is a sign.
explanation.definitionFit: To recruit people is to enlist them, which is what an employer or army does when it signs them up.

clue.text: "Love aid? Bah!" snapped the prophet

indicators.note: something snapped is broken, so the letters are smashed and rebuilt

blocks.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like O
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An Old Testament prophet scoffs at the idea of romantic help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snapped' looks like the verb of speech for the prophet's retort, but it signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Obadiah is a minor Hebrew prophet whose short book is in the Old Testament.

clue.text: House likely to be discontented by this type of crook

definitions.text: House likely to be discontented by this type of crook

blocks.note: surface reading: a household that is unhappy with something
setter's reading: dis-contented, its contents removed, as when a house is stripped by a thief

explanation.walkthrough: Discontented usually means unhappy, but read as dis-contented it means emptied of contents, which is what this crook does to a house.
explanation.definitionFit: A housebreaker breaks into homes and steals their possessions, leaving them stripped of contents.

clue.text: Craft shown by Brenda after Ecstasy-swallowing scare

indicators.note: to swallow something is to take it inside, so one piece holds another
coming after places this piece at the end of the answer

blocks.note: a fright is a scare
E is slang for the drug ecstasy
Brenda is Private Eye's nickname for Queen Elizabeth II, whose royal cipher is ER

explanation.surface: The Queen shows off a handicraft after a drug scare.
explanation.walkthrough: Private Eye has long called the late Queen 'Brenda'; ER stands for Elizabeth Regina. 'Craft' looks like a hobby, but it is a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A freighter is a ship or aircraft that carries cargo, and craft is a general word for vessels.

clue.text: Look serious and admit following French

indicators.note: following means coming after, so this piece goes second

blocks.note: Fr is the abbreviation for French
to own up is to admit, so own means admit

explanation.surface: Put on a grave face and confess to coming after the French.
explanation.walkthrough: FR is the short form of French; 'own' means admit, as in 'I own I was wrong'.
explanation.definitionFit: To frown is to furrow your brow, giving a stern or grave expression.

clue.text: see 6dn.
(& 25/11/12) Avoid getting into debt when effecting a get-together of a couple of arses?

definitions.text: effecting a get-together of a couple of arses

blocks.note: first meaning: the idiom for living within one's income

blocks.clueFragment: effecting a get-together of a couple of arses
blocks.note: second meaning, taken literally: bringing two backsides together

explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning reads the idiom literally: ends are backsides, so making two ends meet is bringing a pair of bottoms together.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means earning just enough to cover your expenses, so you stay out of the red.

clue.text: Brenda and Brian, say, joined secretive member

blocks.note: Brenda is Private Eye's nickname for the Queen, who was mother of Charles
Brian is Private Eye's nickname for Prince Charles, the Queen's son

explanation.surface: Two people named Brenda and Brian sign up to a hush-hush society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' signals examples: Private Eye calls the Queen Brenda and Charles Brian, so they are an example of a mother and son.
explanation.definitionFit: A mason, or Freemason, belongs to a fraternal order famous for its secret rituals and handshakes.

clue.text: see 24ac.
Naive, off limits pics?

indicators.note: something off has gone wrong, so the letters are put out of order

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone innocently asks whether certain photos are forbidden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Off limits' reads as one phrase meaning forbidden, but it splits: 'off' is the signal and 'limits' is part of the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Simplistic means treating complex issues as simpler than they are, an unsophisticated or credulous view.

clue.text: Shout "Pence is in hospital" and scramble

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it

blocks.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat hospital department
a cry is a shout
p is the abbreviation for pence

explanation.surface: A cry goes up that Mike Pence has been hospitalised, and everyone rushes about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pence' looks like the US vice-president, but it is money. Shout and pence together go inside the hospital department.
explanation.definitionFit: To scramble a message is to encode it so only intended recipients can read it, which is what encryption does.

clue.text: Press: "A grand English bygone time"

blocks.note: to iron clothes is to press them
taken as written
G is short for grand, a thousand pounds
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A newspaper nostalgically recalls a great English past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Press' looks like newspapers, but it is the verb for smoothing clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iron Age is the prehistoric period when iron tools came into use, a long-past era.
